group: The Supernatural: The Devil, Demons & Angels
belief: Every problem I have is a spiritual attack.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that every problem you have is a spiritual attack, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: A church culture that blamed the devil for flat tires, illness, and bad moods alike. Frightening teaching about demons that left you watchful and anxious. Wanting an explanation for suffering that does not involve your own choices or ordinary causes. Real experiences of evil that made you suspicious of everything. Feeling helpless, so that an outside enemy seems like the only explanation.
teaches: The devil is real, and Scripture tells us to be alert and resist him. But the Bible also names many other causes of trouble: living in a broken world, our own desires and choices, other people’s choices, and the limits of our human bodies. When Elijah was exhausted and despairing, God sent an angel with food and let him sleep. Jesus said we will have trouble in this world, and He has overcome it.
self_statements: The enemy is behind everything that goes wrong.
If I’m tired or sad, I’m under attack.
I have to fight spiritually every time something breaks.
Nothing bad ever happens by accident.
My choices have nothing to do with my problems.
errors: Turning “the devil sometimes attacks” into “every problem is an attack.”
Deciding the cause before looking at ordinary explanations.
Placing all responsibility outside yourself, so nothing can be changed.
Reading a dark spiritual meaning into everyday trouble.
Overlooking physical, emotional, and practical causes.
questions: What ordinary causes could explain this problem?
Did Jesus say trouble would come only from the devil, or from living in this world?
When Elijah despaired, what did God give him first?
Is there any part of this I can change by my own choices?
Could this be my body asking for rest, food, or medical care?
Does blaming the enemy for everything make me more fearful or more faithful?
How can I resist the devil without seeing him behind every problem?
truth: Not every problem is a spiritual attack. Some trouble comes from a broken world, some from my body, some from my own or other people’s choices, and sometimes from the enemy. I can stay alert without living in fear. Jesus has overcome the world, and I can take each problem to Him and deal with it wisely.
hw_questions: What ordinary causes could explain this?
What did Jesus say about trouble in this world?
What did God give Elijah first?
Is there any part of this I can change?
Could my body need rest, food, or care?
Does blaming the enemy make me more fearful?
hw_truths: Trouble is part of life in this world, and Jesus has overcome it.
Not every problem is a spiritual attack.
I can stay alert without living in fear.
God cares for my body as well as my soul.
I can take each problem to Jesus and handle it wisely.
Greater is He who is in me.
log: When a problem comes, write it down with three possible causes: physical, practical, and spiritual. Then write one wise step.
name_example: I have told Sarah these things so that in Me she may have peace. In the world she will have tribulation. But take courage; I have overcome the world!
actions: and list every possible cause before deciding it is spiritual. Choose one practical step and take it.
Take care of your body for three days:
sleep, eat regular meals, and walk, then notice whether “attacks” change.
and write down how God cared for Elijah’s body before speaking to his soul.
how they tell the difference between spiritual warfare and ordinary trouble.
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that You have overcome the world. Help me reject the lie that every problem is a spiritual attack. Give me wisdom to see the real causes of my troubles, courage to take wise steps, and peace in knowing that You are greater than any enemy. In Your name, Amen.
songs: Bring fear and uncertainty to God rather than carrying the outcome alone.
God’s presence provides courage without requiring a life free of difficulty.
Jesus is the risen Savior and the source of salvation.
This classic hymn connects God’s greatness, Christ’s sacrifice, and future hope.
